title: Map Drawer: Draw, Measure, Export GeoJSON
description: Use the Map Drawer to sketch lines and polygons on the map — lengths, areas and perimeters measured geodesically as you draw, GeoJSON out. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, trace a park's boundary in a dozen clicks and the drawer reports its perimeter and area as you go — a rough fence quote before anyone books a surveyor.
quick_answer: The Map Drawer lets you click to draw lines and polygons directly on the map, measuring as you go: lines report geodesic length, polygons report area and perimeter. When the shape is right, export everything as GeoJSON — drawing, measuring and keeping, all in your browser.

Draw from Times Square to Grand Central Terminal — about 0.91 km as the crow flies. The drawer measures the geodesic, not the walk: the streets you would actually walk add turns the straight line skips.

Four clicks make a polygon; the fifth click closes it. Area appears with the close — and dragging a corner to the real fence line updates it live, which is where rough estimates become defensible ones.

faq: Can I edit a shape after drawing it?
Vertices can be adjusted and shapes removed as you work — get the geometry right before exporting, since the GeoJSON simply records what is on the map at export time.
Lengths and areas switch between metric and imperial — kilometres and miles, hectares and acres — so a fence quote and a land listing can both be served from one drawing.
Can I draw over satellite imagery?

Where the basemap offers an aerial view, drawing over it is the fastest way to trace real fence lines and field edges. The measurements are the map's coordinates, so imagery alignment sets the practical precision.
How do I draw a perfect circle?
A polygon with many close vertices approximates one; for a true radius shape, the dedicated radius tools (Map Radius and friends) draw exact circles the drawer deliberately does not fake.
Can I import a shape to edit?
Bring existing geometry in through the GeoJSON Viewer ecosystem or redraw it here — the drawer is primarily a creation tool, and redrawing a simple boundary takes a minute.
No — it is surface area on the ellipsoid (the map's footprint), not the true sloping ground area. Hillside parcels measure larger in boots than on paper; surveyors handle that distinction.
Can I measure in a straight line between two far cities?
You can draw it, and the geodesic length will be the great-circle distance — the same answer the distance calculators give, with the line visible for free.
